clue.text: Zone taking a hit that should be marked on relief map?

definitions.text: Zone taking a hit that should be marked on relief map?

parts.words: Zone taking a hit that should be marked on relief map
parts.note: a place struck by catastrophe is just where aid agencies would plot their relief efforts, so 'relief map' means a map for disaster relief, not one showing hills

explanation.surface: A cartographer wonders which battered region to shade on a relief map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relief map' suggests contour shading of hills and valleys; here relief is help sent after a catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is officially used for a region struck by catastrophe and declared in need of emergency aid.

clue.text: See doctor, since spasm is unpleasantly severe

parts.note: as can mean since, as in 'as it was raining'
a tic is an involuntary muscle spasm

explanation.surface: A patient with a nasty twitch is told to go and see a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a link inviting the solver to look at the pieces that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Drastic measures are harsh and extreme, forceful in a way that hurts.

clue.text: End of meal-bring round hot German loaf

indicators.note: the word for hot is brought around another letter, enclosing it

parts.note: hot goods are stolen goods

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: At the close of dinner someone brings out a warm German bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' looks like the temperature of the loaf, but it is slang for stolen; L, the end of 'meal', sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stollen is a fruited sweet bread from Germany, traditionally baked at Christmas.

clue.text: Pat, say, that's easy to borrow from

definitions.meaning: a pat is an example of a gentle tap with the hand
a person who readily lends money when asked

explanation.surface: Someone called Pat is known as the friend who will always lend you cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pat' reads as a person's name; it is a light tap, an example of a gentle contact.
explanation.definitionFit: A light tap is a gentle contact, and a person easily persuaded to hand over money is called by the same phrase.

clue.text: Raced up round front of green that damages grass

indicators.note: the reversed word for raced goes round a letter, enclosing it
in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: tore means rushed or raced, as in 'tore down the road'

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Something tears round the front of a golf green, ruining the turf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' turns TORE into EROT, written upwards in this down clue; G from 'green' goes inside to give ER-G-OT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergot is a fungal disease that attacks rye and other cereals and wild grasses.

clue.text: A Latin mistress in comprehensive

parts.note: a mistress is a lover

explanation.surface: A Latin teacher is found working at a comprehensive school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comprehensive' suggests a British state secondary school; here it is the adjective meaning complete.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thorough that covers everything extends across the whole, as in 'all-over tan'.

clue.text: Blow up in general explosion

indicators.note: an explosion blows a word apart so its letters land in a new order

explanation.surface: An army general is caught up in a blast.
explanation.walkthrough: The seven letters of 'general' are rearranged, signalled by 'explosion'.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow up a photograph is to make it bigger.

clue.text: Sporting competition using a series of rings

definitions.text: Sporting competition using a series of rings

parts.words: Sporting competition using a series of rings
parts.note: the event's flag shows five interlocking rings, and gymnasts also compete on rings, so the description fits the world's biggest multi-sport festival

explanation.surface: A contest built around a run of rings, perhaps for boxing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rings' could suggest boxing rings or ring tosses; it is the five-ring emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: The international multi-sport festival's emblem is five interlocking coloured circles.

clue.text: Start with what burglar wants from church roof

definitions.meaning: to begin something, as in opening a discussion

definitions.text: what burglar wants from church roof
definitions.meaning: thieves strip metal sheeting off church roofs to sell, so they want it removed

explanation.surface: A thief begins the night by eyeing the roofing on the local church.
explanation.walkthrough: Church roofs are traditionally covered in sheet metal, which thieves strip and sell.
explanation.definitionFit: To open proceedings is to go first; separately, a thief wants the metal sheeting taken from the roof.

clue.text: Girl I shelter in porch

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: A girl takes cover from the weather in a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link. The definition is the church sense: a chapel or porch at the west end of some cathedrals.
explanation.definitionFit: In church architecture the name is given to a porch or chapel at the entrance of a cathedral, as at Durham and Ely.

clue.text: One veteran surprisingly came-six, never

indicators.note: surprisingly signals that the letters turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A veteran remarks with surprise that he finished sixth and never better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprisingly' rearranges the twelve letters of 'came six never'.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran is a person who formerly served in the armed forces.

clue.text: Friend meets fate as sailor

parts.note: a mate is a friend
one's lot in life is one's fate

explanation.surface: A friend accepts their destiny on going to sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meets' is a link joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Matelot is British slang, from French, for a seaman in the navy.

clue.text: Servant drunk in pubs

indicators.note: being drunk muddles things, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A servant is found intoxicated in the local bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' rearranges the letters of 'Servant'.
explanation.definitionFit: Taverns are inns or public houses serving drink.

clue.text: Old American safely recorded?

definitions.meaning: one of the people of the pre-Columbian empire of Peru
film safely shot is said to be in the can, read here as two words

explanation.surface: A pre-Columbian native has had his story securely captured on tape.
explanation.walkthrough: Film makers say a finished scene is 'in the can'; split as IN CAN the answer means recorded.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the Andean empire's people; split in two, the words echo the film-set phrase for completed shooting.

clue.text: Drowned Durham girl found here, in scanty clothing?

definitions.text: Drowned Durham girl found here, in scanty clothing?

parts.words: Drowned Durham girl found here, in scanty clothing
parts.note: the Wear is the river flowing through the city of Durham, so a drowned girl there would be found beneath its water; the same words split differently name intimate garments

explanation.surface: A grim news story about a girl from Durham pulled from the water, barely dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wear is the river running through Durham in north-east England; split as UNDER WEAR the answer says where the drowned girl lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Briefs, knickers and similar intimate garments are skimpy items worn beneath outer clothes.

clue.text: It's good to sink doubles and trebles here in pub

definitions.text: It's good to sink doubles and trebles here in pub

parts.words: It's good to sink doubles and trebles here in pub
parts.note: doubles and trebles sound like drinks to sink, but they are the scoring rings a player aims for in the classic pub game with flights

explanation.surface: A drinker recommends knocking back double and triple measures at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doubles and trebles' suggest drinks; in darts they are the rings scoring two or three times the number.
explanation.definitionFit: The target in darts has double and treble rings where a thrown arrow scores extra.

clue.text: Sponsor of film title role

definitions.meaning: a person who vouches for a child at baptism
Coppola's 1972 film is named after Don Corleone's role

explanation.surface: Someone backs a movie in which the star plays the part named in its title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of' is a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A baptismal sponsor stands for a child at christening, and Coppola's mafia film takes its name from Don Corleone's role.

clue.text: Appointment to go round hospital department showing toothy appearance

indicators.note: the word for appointment goes round the department, enclosing it

parts.note: a date is an arranged appointment
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: A patient has an appointment in a hospital ward and leaves grinning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To go round' is the container signal; ENT, the ear, nose and throat department, is a standard hospital abbreviation solvers meet often.
explanation.definitionFit: A dentate leaf or edge is notched with tooth-like points.

clue.text: A reason not to be sailing?

parts.note: grounds are reasons, as in 'grounds for divorce'

explanation.surface: A sailor offers an excuse for staying in port.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as an excuse; the definition is the end: a ship stuck on the bottom is not sailing.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship stuck on the seabed or a sandbank cannot move under way.

clue.text: I put on fur-from this?

indicators.note: placed on the end, so the letter follows the word for fur

parts.note: an animal's fur is its coat

explanation.surface: A wearer of a fur wonders which animal supplied it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a raccoon-like animal from the Americas whose pelt might make a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: The coati is a long-snouted, ringed-tailed mammal of the raccoon family with a furry pelt.

clue.text: Appeal to join in barbarous campaign

indicators.note: the appeal is made to join the other word by going inside it

parts.note: crude means rough and uncivilised, like barbarous
SA stands for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Someone calls on people to join a savage military drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appeal' alone stands for sex appeal, a crossword convention; 'to join in' tells it to go inside the word for barbarous.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusade is a vigorous drive for a cause, after the medieval holy wars.

clue.text: Discharges bill and resigns

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill
quits means leaves a job, resigns

explanation.surface: Someone pays off a debt and walks out of their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' is a link joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A court that acquits a defendant declares them not guilty and releases them.

clue.text: Someturnedbackafterfellow's threat to intruders

indicators.note: the reversed piece comes after the word for fellow

parts.note: a man is a fellow

indicators.note: the clue's 'turned back' (printed run together) says the word for some is read from right to left

parts.note: part means some, as in 'part of the cake'

explanation.surface: A man turns round on hearing someone warn off trespassers.
explanation.walkthrough: The feed prints the first words run together; read as 'Some turned back after fellow's', where 'turned back' gives TRAP and 'after' puts it behind the fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantrap is a hidden snare set on private land to catch trespassers.

clue.text: It holds power all across the countryside

definitions.text: It holds power all across the countryside

parts.words: It holds power all across the countryside
parts.note: power reads as political control, but means electricity, carried on tall steel towers marching over fields

explanation.surface: A ruling party keeps control of every rural region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holds power' suggests political authority; it is the lattice tower holding electricity cables.
explanation.definitionFit: Steel lattice towers carry high-voltage electricity lines across open land.

clue.text: Abrupt start from barrister with trick question thrown in

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter
a piece is thrown into the word for trick, landing inside it

parts.note: a ruse is a trick

explanation.surface: A barrister's tricky question in cross-examination makes for a curt exchange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start from' takes the first letter of 'barrister'; 'thrown in' puts the question abbreviation inside the trick, not a courtroom ploy.
explanation.definitionFit: A brusque manner is curt and blunt, short to the point of rudeness.

clue.text: Flier for Chekhov production

definitions.meaning: something that flies, here a bird of the coast

explanation.surface: Someone flies out to see a staging of a Russian play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' is a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A gull is a coastal bird that flies, and Chekhov's play is named after one.

clue.text: A chap takes something — a mushroom

parts.note: a man is a chap
it can stand for something unnamed, as in 'there's it again'

explanation.surface: A man swallows something and it turns out to be a fungus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes' is a link; the pieces follow in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Amanita is the genus including the fly agaric and death cap, many poisonous.

clue.text: Expensive costume for a once-in-a lifetime give-away?

definitions.text: Expensive costume for a once-in-a lifetime give-away?

parts.words: Expensive costume for a once-in-a lifetime give-away
parts.note: a bride is given away by her father, so the costume is the costly gown worn on that day

explanation.surface: A pricey outfit is offered as a prize in a one-off giveaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give-away' suggests a free offer; it is the bride being given away at her marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride usually wears a costly white gown at her marriage ceremony, often worn only once.
